novelty_signal: Strongest surviving bridge. The claim only survives as helper-free pre-arbitration source scouting under mixed polarity and impedance asymmetry; it is structurally distinct from single-source startup and steady-state multi-input extraction, but still unproven on measured performance.
validation_plan: Run the frozen H1 matrix on variant_01_rc_ranked_packet_gate across 20/50/100/300 mV, 0.1/1/10/100 mV/s, 1:1/1:5/1:20 impedance ratios, and mixed-polarity cases. Compare against both fixed_startup_path and nonaware_multi_input_startup, then add source-collapse and leaky-path adversarial cases. Promote only if startup_ok or t_handoff improves without e_ctrl and e_backdrive blowing up.
risk: RC recovery signatures may collapse under ultra-slow ramps, and if the nonaware baseline shows negligible back-drive this bridge shrinks to extra logic with better accounting rather than a publishable new startup mechanism.

novelty_signal: Mixed-polarity isolation remains the cleanest differentiation against recent collaborative multi-input interfaces, and the current anomaly notes say bucketed polarity handling becomes more attractive at extreme 1:20 asymmetry plus mixed polarity.
validation_plan: Evaluate only on mixed-polarity primary cases. Measure startup_ok, t_handoff, e_backdrive, and merge-control energy against the champion root and both baselines. Keep it promoted only if polarity-safe merge prevents wrong-way startup without turning either bucket into a de facto helper reservoir.
risk: Bucket leakage and merge overhead are likely to dominate below 50 mV, collapsing the benefit into a slower and leakier version of a simpler startup path.

novelty_signal: Useful as the cleanest source-awareness ablation, but multiple artifacts say it is too close to ordinary RC arbitration to anchor the headline claim.
validation_plan: Use it as the required control. Hold source voltages equal, sweep 1:1 to 1:20 impedances, and compare benefit per control energy versus packet_scout_handoff_root. Keep only if it establishes a strong lower-complexity baseline for the source-awareness argument.
risk: Under ultra-slow ramps the fast and slow RC signatures may collapse, making the ranking too noisy to prove novelty or even to serve as a decisive benchmark.

novelty_signal: Not a standalone novelty bridge, but it may become mandatory if mixed-polarity cases trigger UVLO chatter. It is best treated as a support block inside H1 rather than as a paper claim.
validation_plan: Inject threshold-oscillation and half-enable cases into the champion matrix. Keep it only if token gating removes chatter or false handoff that ordinary hysteresis misses under equal control-energy accounting.
risk: The token chain can become a disguised helper or control rail and erase the energy advantage while reading like a conventional POR or UVLO deglitcher.

novelty_signal: Weak. Anti-backdrive is already expected in multi-input interfaces, and the leakage-vote framing looks more like fragile sensing around existing OR-ing devices than a differentiated architecture.
validation_plan: Retire as a standalone bridge. Only resurrect it if a later source-collapse matrix shows a large startup-correctness gap that simpler isolation cannot close.
risk: Process and temperature spread can swamp leakage signatures, turning the bridge into calibration-heavy cosmetics with little startup benefit.

novelty_signal: Low confidence. It was already downgraded to a conditional merge candidate, the specific minimum-energy probe question ended in a parse error, and the bridge survives only if it beats the RC ranker without hidden bias or precharge.
validation_plan: Retire as a standalone branch. Absorb it only as a sub-block experiment inside packet_scout_handoff_root after the RC-ranked variant is benchmarked. Re-open only if measured probe energy is clearly below the RC ranker while preserving startup correctness.
